subject: Data Structures & Algorithms (CST 201)
question_text: Define a Stack Abstract Data Type (ADT). Explain the primary operations PUSH and POP with their time complexities, and state one real-world application.
ideal_answer: A Stack is a linear data structure following the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle. The primary operations are: 1. PUSH: inserts an element to the top of the stack with O(1) time complexity; 2. POP: removes and returns the top element from the stack with O(1) time complexity. It also supports PEEK to view the top element. Real-world applications include function call management / recursion stack in compilers, undo/redo operations in text editors, and syntax parsing / balanced parentheses checking.
student_answer: A stack is a linear data structure operating under the LIFO (Last In First Out) principle, where insertions and deletions happen only at one end called the top. The two core operations are: PUSH which places an item on top of the stack in O(1) constant time, and POP which extracts the topmost element from the stack in O(1) time complexity. A real-world application is the execution call stack in runtime environments to manage function calls and recursion.
human_rationale: Comprehensive, accurate answer addressing all rubric criteria with correct time complexities.

subject: Database Management Systems (CST 202)
question_text: Explain the ACID properties of database transactions and describe the importance of Atomicity and Durability.
ideal_answer: ACID properties ensure reliable processing of database transactions: 1. Atomicity: The all-or-nothing property; either all operations succeed or the transaction is rolled back; 2. Consistency: Database transitions from one valid state to another, satisfying all integrity constraints; 3. Isolation: Concurrent transactions execute independently without interference; 4. Durability: Once a transaction commits, its updates persist permanently even across power failures or system crashes.
student_answer:
ACID properties define transaction guarantees in DBMS:
1. Atomicity: Transactions are atomic (all-or-nothing). If a failure occurs before completion, all partial changes are rolled back.
2. Consistency: Transactions maintain database integrity rules and constraints.
3. Isolation: Multiple concurrent transactions occur independently without viewing intermediate dirty states.
4. Durability: Committed data is permanently saved in non-volatile storage and survives system crashes.
Atomicity prevents partial writes (e.g. money debited but not credited). Durability ensures committed state is never lost even if the server reboots.
human_rationale: Complete and accurate description of ACID properties with proper failure/recovery mechanisms.

subject: Basic Electrical Engineering (EST 100)
question_text: State Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) and calculate the total equivalent resistance of three resistors (10 ohms, 20 ohms, and 20 ohms) connected in parallel.
ideal_answer: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) states that the algebraic sum of all currents entering and leaving a junction or node in an electrical circuit is equal to zero (sum of entering currents equals sum of leaving currents). For three resistors in parallel: 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3 = 1/10 + 1/20 + 1/20 = 2/20 + 1/20 + 1/20 = 4/20 = 1/5. Therefore, R_eq = 5 Ohms.
student_answer: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) states that the algebraic sum of currents meeting at any node is zero; current entering equals current leaving. For parallel connection, 1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3 = 1/10 + 1/20 + 1/20 = 4/20 = 1/5. Req = 5 Ohms (5 Ω).
human_rationale: Flawless statement of KCL and exact parallel resistance computation with units.

subject: Constitution of India (EST 130)
question_text: Explain the Right to Constitutional Remedies under Article 32 and describe any three prerogative writs issued by the Supreme Court.
ideal_answer: Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, regarded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. It empowers citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Three prerogative writs are: 1. Habeas Corpus: 'To have the body', issued against illegal detention to produce a detained person; 2. Mandamus: 'We command', directs a public official or authority to perform a mandatory statutory duty; 3. Quo-Warranto: 'By what authority', inquires into the legality of a person's claim to a public office.
student_answer: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies and was called the heart and soul of the Constitution by Dr. Ambedkar. It gives citizens the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Three writs are: 1. Habeas Corpus: meaning 'to have the body', issued to release individuals illegally detained by state or private actors. 2. Mandamus: meaning 'we command', ordering a public official to perform their official legal duty. 3. Quo Warranto: questioning 'by what authority' an individual holds a public office.
human_rationale: Comprehensive explanation of Article 32 and accurate descriptions of all three writs.

subject: Industrial Economics & Foreign Trade (HUT 300)
question_text: Explain the concept of Price Elasticity of Demand (PED), write its formula, and distinguish between Elastic and Inelastic demand.
ideal_answer: Price Elasticity of Demand (PED) measures the responsiveness or sensitivity of the quantity demanded of a good to a change in its price. Formula: e_p = (% change in quantity demanded) / (% change in price). Elastic demand occurs when |e_p| > 1, meaning quantity demanded changes by a greater proportion than price (flatter demand curve, luxury goods). Inelastic demand occurs when |e_p| < 1, meaning quantity demanded changes by a smaller proportion than price (steeper demand curve, necessities like salt or life-saving medicines).
student_answer: Price Elasticity of Demand measures the degree of responsiveness of quantity demanded to changes in the price of a commodity. Formula: PED = (% change in quantity demanded) / (% change in price). Demand is Elastic when PED > 1, meaning consumers are very responsive and a small price rise causes a large drop in demand (e.g. luxury items). Demand is Inelastic when PED < 1, meaning consumer demand changes very little when price changes (e.g. basic necessities like salt and medicines).
human_rationale: Clear definition, exact percentage formula, and proper comparison with examples.

ideal_answer: KCL: Point rule, sum of currents is zero. Req = 5 Ohms.
